02-mozilla.title: Mozilla: 85 languages, no sitemap.
02-mozilla.alt: Real run, worldwide card. Mozilla: 85 languages, no sitemap. Overall score 86 of 100. SEO 73, GEO 86, Analytics 85, Security 89, A11y 86, Speed 94. www.mozilla.org, 20 pages analyzed, 19 Oct 2026.
02-mozilla.linkedin:
Mozilla: 85 languages, no sitemap.

The home page lists 85 hreflang alternates, HSTS is on, and framing is denied. But robots.txt names no sitemap and /sitemap.xml answers 404, so crawlers find pages only by following links.

The lesson for every team: Publish a sitemap.xml of the pages you want found and name it in robots.txt with one Sitemap: line.

05-unesco.title: UNESCO has llms.txt, but no HSTS.
05-unesco.alt: Real run, worldwide card. UNESCO has llms.txt, but no HSTS. Overall score 70 of 100. SEO 67, GEO 56, Analytics 85, Security 62, A11y 89, Speed 68. www.unesco.org, 20 pages analyzed, 19 Oct 2026.
05-unesco.linkedin:
UNESCO has llms.txt, but no HSTS.

UNESCO publishes an llms.txt for AI tools, sets a content security policy, and limits framing to itself. But no page analyzed sends Strict-Transport-Security, and http:// moves to https with a temporary 302.

The lesson for every team: Send Strict-Transport-Security with a max-age of a year or more, and make the http-to-https hop a 301.

One automated analysis of public pages on 19 Oct 2026. A starting point, not a verdict.

06-unicef.title: UNICEF's date filter has no label.
06-unicef.alt: Real run, worldwide card. UNICEF's date filter has no label. Overall score 84 of 100. SEO 86, GEO 91, Analytics 85, Security 88, A11y 85, Speed 67. www.unicef.org, 20 pages analyzed, 19 Oct 2026.
06-unicef.linkedin:
UNICEF's date filter has no label.

Preloaded HSTS, Organization JSON-LD, and five language versions linked to each other. But the search date filter on every page analyzed is named only by placeholder text, which vanishes as you type.

The lesson for every team: Give every field a <label> or an aria-label. A placeholder is a hint, not a name, and it disappears on input.

One automated analysis of public pages on 19 Oct 2026. A starting point, not a verdict.

08-icrc.linkedin:
The ICRC tests a CSP. Now it can enforce it.

A security.txt for researchers, a sitemap named in robots.txt, and HSTS. Its content security policy runs in report-only mode, so the browser logs violations but blocks nothing.

The lesson for every team: Read the reports for a few weeks, fix what they flag, then switch the header to Content-Security-Policy.

30-rijksmuseum.linkedin:

A Permissions-Policy, a Referrer-Policy, nosniff, and a sitemap named in robots.txt. But Strict-Transport-Security sets max-age to 30 days, and http:// reaches https through a temporary 307.

68-uniandes.linkedin:
Uniandes skips a link in its TLS chain.

HSTS, a CSP from default-src 'self', nosniff, and a Permissions-Policy. But the server sends its certificate twice and leaves out the DigiCert intermediate. Browsers patch it in; Node.js and API clients refuse.
